# Fighting the Grand Machine
The Grand Machine fights from inside the colony. Its servants look like the Working Joes everyone trusts, so the hardest part is knowing who to fight.
## Spotting Them - [bold]A freighter at the landing zone.[/bold] A Seegson shipment of Working Joes landing unannounced, then leaving minutes later, is a warning in itself. Count the new Joes. - [bold]Joes where they should not be[/bold], or doing nothing a Joe would do, especially alone with someone. - [bold]People found asleep or dead with ruined lungs.[/bold] A drowned victim has damaged lungs, often with no other wound. A forensic scanner can tell you more. See [textlink="Forensics" link="CMUGuideForensics"]. - [bold]Consoles locking up[/bold], cameras going dark, communications failing, or lights burning out across a district. APOLLO reports assimilated consoles. - [bold]Early Warning Joes give themselves away[/bold] as they grow. At CHORUS the Colonial Marshals are faxed a line-up and the Joe looks wrong on close examination. At MELDING, APOLLO warns everyone and the Joe glows. - Any colony synthetic that suddenly acts out of character may have been melded into the River.
## Fighting Them - Working Joes take a lot of damage and hit hard. Do not fight one alone or unarmed. - [bold]None of them can fire guns.[/bold] Keep your distance and shoot. - Do not let one grab you. A grab is how a drowning starts. Moving away or hurting the Joe breaks a Drown. - An Early Warning Joe can jam every gun around it, silence sentries, blind a crowd with a flash, and leap between levels. Approach from more than one side, and do not bunch up. - When an Early Warning Joe overheats, its abilities stop working. Press it then. - An Early Warning Joe may come back if the River kept a copy of it. Keep watching after it falls.
## Repairing Them - A [bold]reset key[/bold] used on a hijacked Joe or a River-Melded thrall frees it from the Grand Machine. Every Working Joe carries a Seegson reset key. - A dead Working Joe repaired to full health can be [bold]rebooted[/bold] from its context menu. This also frees a hijacked Joe. - A freed Joe is an ordinary Working Joe again, and its player is no longer an antagonist. - Early Warning Joes cannot be repaired this way. They have to be stopped. - A freed Joe that dies can be hijacked again. Keep dead synthetics away from the Grand Machine's servants, or repair them quickly.
## Dealing With the Aftermath - [bold]Drowned victims[/bold] are asleep with damaged lungs. Get them to medical fast and treat the lungs, and any suffocation that follows. See [textlink="Organs" link="CMUGuideMedicalOrgans"]. - Assimilated consoles are locked and their data is corrupted. - Lights, headsets and power cells burned out by Disrupt need replacing or recharging. - Weapons hit by Unwind are jammed with their safety on and the magazine out. Pick the magazine up, reload, rack the gun and switch the safety off. - Missing blood at a crime scene is not proof that nothing happened there. An Early Warning Joe can draw blood into itself.
## How the Colony Wins Against a Working Joes shipment, the colony wins once every Joe the shipment brought or converted is dead or gone from the planet. A repaired Joe stops counting against you. If 65% of the colonists are lost, evacuation opens. At 85%, the Grand Machine has won.
